Synopsis:
    Reuters poll shows near-unanimous economist consensus (97%) for a BOJ rate hike to 1.25% on Sept 18, with the terminal rate path accelerating — 1.75% now expected by end-Q2 2027, three months earlier than prior forecasts. Key drivers: persistent inflation, yen weakness at 40-year lows, and notably, explicit US political pressure via Treasury Secretary Bessent endorsing BOJ tightening. A coordinated US-Japan yen intervention has lowered political resistance to hikes. Fiscal risk is also flagged, with Japan's budget requests swelling to pandemic-era levels under PM Takaichi's expansionary agenda, raising JGB issuance concerns.
